title.label: Best Bookmark Manager at This Price Level

content.label: I’ve been using this app for over a month now and once you dig into all the features/ customization options and tune everything to your liking, the app really does shine. It has a lot of functionality.

So I have been using this application for almost two months now and it’s pretty awesome. It is definitely the prettiest and very stable stable bookmarking application that I have used. It is able to take in multiple formats and allows you to keep track of your bookmarks/notes/files/images that you put in it. It’s also very well integrated with the OS as you can share from any app directly to Anybox. However there is a fundamental way in which this application works that is keeping it from reaching it to its fullest potential and that is organization.

In most bookmark applications and browsers (in any application that works with imported items really) the primary way bookmarks are organized is through a folder system. Meaning you can group multiple bookmarks together to put them in folders and even nest multiple folders in one another. From safari to chrome, this is how they work. The more advanced bookmark applications allow you to then tag these bookmarks as a secondary form of organization, you can then select this tag and everything you’ve attached it to shows up (think Finder in macOS)

However Anybox skips the primary form of organization using folders and instead goes directly to the secondary form, tagging which is called “collections” here. Essentially, all the files that you import into the application are all placed in a single directory and the only way that you can organize them is by putting them into these “collections” (There is a useful smart list feature but that works more like an advanced filter than anything else.) Because it lacks the fundamental ability to group its items into folders, browsing through the base “links” page is inherently messy. More so if you import your bookmarks and already had them organized elsewhere.

My only request now is that a folder organization system be added to the app. From there, nesting folders can be included. iCloud can be used for this, simply by having a default Anybox folder there and everything imported can retain its hierarchy for the main application to browse through. This will also come in handy when exporting items. Since bookmark files are so small, users could store a lot there. I think if this application does this, it will really dominate. The only real competitor it has is URL manager. I recommend the devs take a look at it.

A lesser function that I think would be useful for this app is privacy enhancement. For one, people may store sensitive links in this app so it would be good to have someway to protect that, either by password protecting the app all together or specific sections in it. For another, it would be good to allow users to decide if these want specified sensitive bookmarks to appear in searches or not. Don’t need your kid to run a spotlight search for “x-men” and see results for other things, if you know what I mean.

Despite all I’ve said, I really really do like this app. So much so that I have bought a lifetime license. I see a lot of potential in it. It’s new and growing. It doesn’t have many proper reviews which is why I’m writing this as proper feedback to the Devs. I hope they are able to sort out the lack of folder organization so the pro users can really kick this thing into high gear. Cause it definitely can be a powerful app if given the right features.

title.label: The bookmarking tool I always wanted to build

I spent years keeping a modest collection of bookmarks in Pinboard and Raindrop, but ironically I only ever wanted a great native desktop experience for my bookmarks.

Anybox covers just about every use case I have and then some. It avoids the trap of becoming yet another read-it-later app while providing great productivity features like AppleScript support and deeplinking. The drag-and-drop support makes importing and exporting a breeze as well.

All in all, a fantastic app with a receptive developer and flexible subscription and one time payment options for just about everyone.
